es-step-size-adaptation

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:es-step-size-adaptation` → `ai-es-step-size-adaptation` → `src/demos/ai/ai-es-step-size-adaptation`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/180`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30f.md#7-es-step-size-adaptation`. **Packet:** E1. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:evolution-strategies`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** evolution-strategies fixes offsets; this computes success fraction and actually changes the next search scale under a declared rule.

**Computed primary model:** Objective score−(x−1)², center0 score−1, four standardized offsets[−1,−.5,.5,1]. Multiply bysigma. sigma.1 probes[−.1,−.05,.05,.1], strict improvements2/4; sigma4 probes[−4,−2,2,4], strict improvements0/4 (x2 only ties current score). Rule fraction>.2 doubles nextsigma; fraction<.2 halves it, otherwise unchanged. Next scales.2 and2. Best strict-improvement moves center to.1 versus staying0.

**Countercase / boundary:** At optimal center1 no probe strictly improves, so the rule shrinks even if all movement is useless. This fixed four-probe success-rule analogue is not complete CMA-ES cumulative step adaptation, a sampled expected success rate or convergence guarantee.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict next scale after the oversize4 probe set; recall ties are not successes and shrinking alone does not prove a better next candidate.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Try scale/Adapt scale computes positions, scores, success fraction and nextsigma; Move center to optimum exposes the boundary. Retain small versus large-scale actual movement and score evidence.
